director.chapterArc: A tense confrontation where the group forces Rook to reveal his secrets in exchange for a dangerous trade: visibility via a massive fire.
director.restraintNote: Maintain Toren's analytical distance throughout; let the emotional weight land through silence and pacing rather than vocal strain. Character voices must remain distinct but grounded, never melodramatic.

cues.delivery: Narrator's realization of Rook's refusal; measured and analytical.
cues.from: He was, in short, entirely available to all of them, all day, about everything, and Toren understood on the shafts at about four in the afternoon that this was the most complete refusal he had ever been given by anybody.
cues.through: He was, in short, entirely available to all of them, all day, about everything, and Toren understood on the shafts at about four in the afternoon that this was the most complete refusal he had ever been given by anybody.

cues.delivery: Rook's brief dialogue; flat and utilitarian.
Toren observing the shift in Rook; precise and observant.
cues.from: Rook's eyes went to him and stopped.
cues.through: Toren, who had spent twenty-eight days learning to watch this man for the size of a thing crossing his face, saw one go across that was bigger than any of the others. It was not fast, either. It stayed.
cues.reason: Highlighting a subtle but significant character beat.

cues.delivery: Dialogue between Rook and Dessa; calm correction.
Dessa laying out facts; flat and factual.
cues.from: "And you went over sideways against a wheel at twenty past one, and you have not told us why you can't sleep. Those are the facts. We're not asking for an apology and we're not frightened of you."
cues.through: And he walked to the gap.
"That's four minutes," he said. "I've done my part of it."

cues.from: "Right," he said. "Then I'll make you an offer, and I want you all to understand before I make it that it is not a trick and it is not less than it sounds."
cues.through: "I'd turn it down tonight. I'd like it tomorrow, please, all of it, and I'll write it on the slate."

cues.delivery: Rook's confrontation with Toren; sharp and personal.
cues.from: The third one was ugly. It was over in about fifteen seconds, and Toren was the one it happened to.
cues.through: Toren sat on the other side of a fire with his face burning and his ears full of blood and discovered that the worst part of it was that about a third of it was true.

cues.delivery: Toren revealing the disk; quiet and deliberate.
cues.from: "That was beneath me," Rook said. "I'd take it back if there were any way of doing that. There isn't, and I'm not going to dress it up. I'm sorry."
cues.through: Nine fine channels running in from the rim, stopping a hair short of the middle. A small ring of nothing. A leather cord somebody had knotted through it in a house, at a table, in the light, four weeks and a lifetime ago.

cues.delivery: Wyck's final accusation; quiet and devastating.
cues.from: "Eleven days ago you sat down on a coping stone," Wyck said, "and you told me you were wrong."
Senna said the last of it, from the cart, in the voice she used for reading out the weather.
cues.through: "That's all," Senna said. "It's not a claim and you don't owe me it. It's just that I've got the shortest road of anybody at this fire, and I'd rather not go down it with a stranger."
cues.reason: The moral weight of the scene.
